class.name: NNBTRoot
class.brief_description: The main node for the Noodle Nodes Behaviour Tree nodes.
class.description: This is the main node for the Noodle Nodes Behaviour Tree nodes. The root node is ticked to update the state of the behaviour tree. The root must have exactly one enabled behaviour tree child. It ticks the first enabled child and returns that child's result. Any further enabled behaviour tree children are ignored; the first time the root is ticked with more than one enabled behaviour tree child it reports a one-time error. The editor shows a configuration warning for the same configuration. [NNSensors] child nodes are allowed in addition to the single behaviour tree child. Sensors do not count as behaviour tree children. If no behaviour tree child is enabled, or the root has no children at all, [method tick] returns [code]FAILURE[/code]. [member blackboard] is the explicitly assigned [NNBlackboard]. When it is null the root uses a private per-instance board, so the blackboard helpers still work without any setup. Assigning [code]null[/code] clears the assignment and falls back to that private board. Blackboards default to [code]resource_local_to_scene = true[/code], so a board assigned in the inspector is duplicated per scene instance unless you deliberately untick that to share one board. [member actor] is the explicitly assigned actor or [code]null[/code]. [member actor] does not store a resolved fallback; read the resolved actor with [method get_actor], which resolves on demand: the live explicit actor wins, then the node at [member actor_node_path], then the root's parent. Because resolution is computed on demand, entering the tree or reparenting re-resolves naturally, and a freed explicit actor falls through to the path or parent. Disabling the root interrupts its active run and resets the whole tree, so re-enabling it starts a fresh run on the next tick. Every reset of the root (including the reset triggered by a child order change) interrupts the active subtree as well. Automatic ticking is opt-in: [member auto_tick] defaults to [code]false[/code], which leaves manual ticking exactly as before. While it is enabled, the selected [member process_thread] callback ticks the tree once per eligible frame without any script call. Only the selected [member process_thread] callback is enabled on the root node. A script attached to the root therefore cannot rely on its own [code]_process[/code] or [code]_physics_process[/code] callback: the root owns that callback, and only the root's chosen callback runs. [constant MANUAL] disables both callbacks so a custom scheduler can call the tree. [member tick_rate] counts eligible invocations of the selected callback, starting with the first one. A rate of 2 ticks on invocations 1, 3, 5 and so on. No wall-clock time is involved. Re-arming the schedule (changing [member auto_tick], [member tick_rate], [member process_thread] or [member is_enabled], entering the tree or resetting the tree) restarts the count so the next eligible invocation is due. Disabling resets the tree, so enabling starts a fresh run. [signal tree_enabled] and [signal tree_disabled] are emitted only on a real transition of [member is_enabled], never when the root merely leaves the tree. [method get_running_action] returns the deepest node on the active path after the last tick, or [code]null[/code] when nothing is active. When parallel nodes have several active children, the first active child in child order wins. The node is stored as an object ID, so if the active node was freed the method returns [code]null[/code] and never returns a freed object.

constants.constant: The root is ticked automatically from [code]_process[/code] while [member auto_tick] is enabled.
The root is ticked automatically from [code]_physics_process[/code] while [member auto_tick] is enabled. This is the default.
Neither callback is enabled and the root never ticks automatically, so a custom scheduler calls [method tick] or [method auto_tick_step] itself.

method.name: auto_tick_step
method.description: The shared body of the [code]_process[/code] and [code]_physics_process[/code] callbacks, and the deterministic driver for custom schedulers. Ticks the tree with [member tick_argument] and the supplied [param delta] when the call is due, and returns [code]true[/code] only when it actually ticked. The call is ignored, returning [code]false[/code], when [param process_thread] is not the selected [member process_thread], when the selected thread is [constant MANUAL], when [member auto_tick] is disabled or the root is disabled, in the editor, or when [member tick_rate] makes this invocation not due. An ignored call does not advance the [member tick_rate] schedule.

method.name: get_assigned_actor
method.description: Returns the explicitly assigned actor, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned or the assigned actor was freed. This is the value of [member actor]. Use [method get_actor] to read the resolved actor.

method.name: get_assigned_blackboard
method.description: Returns the explicitly assigned blackboard, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned. This is the value of [member blackboard]. Use [method NNBTNodes.get_blackboard_resource] to read the effective board, which is the assigned board or this root's private board.

method.name: get_running_action
method.description: Returns the deepest node on the active path after the last tick, or [code]null[/code] when nothing is active. The active path follows the enabled children that the last tick left running: every node on it is enabled, has an internal status of ticked and has a tick result of [code]RUNNING[/code]. When a parallel node has several active children, the first active child in child order wins. The node is tracked through an object ID, so the method returns [code]null[/code] when the active node was freed and never returns a freed object.

method.name: tick
method.description: This is the behaviour tree tick-method you should be using to tick the tree. You can provide any [Variant] type as a parameter (usually a node used as an actor or a dictionary used as a blackboard), along with a delta-time. These are passed to all the child nodes of the behaviour tree during ticks. Manual ticking keeps working while [member auto_tick] is enabled, so a script may call this method and also let the automatic callback tick the tree.

members.member: The explicitly assigned actor, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned. No resolved fallback is ever stored here. To read the resolved actor use [method get_actor], which resolves the explicit actor, then [member actor_node_path], then the root's parent on demand.
Fallback actor path, used when no live explicit [member actor] is set. The path is resolved relative to this root.

When [code]true[/code], the selected [member process_thread] callback ticks the tree automatically. Defaults to [code]false[/code], which leaves the root exactly as before and ticks only through [method tick]. Setting this property re-arms the [member tick_rate] schedule.

The explicitly assigned typed behaviour tree blackboard resource, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned. When it is [code]null[/code] the root uses a private per-instance board and the [NNBTNodes] blackboard helpers still work. Assigning [code]null[/code] clears the assignment and falls back to that private board. Blackboards default to [code]resource_local_to_scene = true[/code], so an assigned inspector board is per scene instance unless you deliberately untick it to share one board. This property is the assignment only; [method NNBTNodes.get_blackboard_resource] returns the effective board.

The callback that drives automatic ticking and the only process callback enabled on the root. Defaults to [constant PHYSICS]. [constant IDLE] uses [code]_process[/code], [constant PHYSICS] uses [code]_physics_process[/code] and [constant MANUAL] disables both so a custom scheduler ticks the tree. Out-of-range values fall back to [constant PHYSICS]. Setting this property re-arms the [member tick_rate] schedule.
The [Variant] passed as the first argument of every automatic tick. It defaults to [code]null[/code]. Manual calls to [method tick] pass their own argument.

The number of eligible invocations of the selected [member process_thread] callback between automatic ticks. The default of [code]1[/code] ticks every eligible invocation, and a rate of 2 ticks on invocations 1, 3, 5 and so on. Values below 1 are clamped to 1. Ineligible invocations, such as those for a callback that is not selected, do not advance the count. Setting this property re-arms the schedule.
This is the total time in microseconds the call to the [method tick] method used.

signal.name: tree_disabled
signal.description: Emitted when the root is disabled through [member is_enabled], after the tree was reset and the process mode was applied. Emitted only on a real transition, so disabling an already disabled root does not emit again.

signal.name: tree_enabled
signal.description: Emitted when the root is re-enabled through [member is_enabled], after the whole tree was reset, so the next tick starts a fresh run. Emitted only on a real transition, so enabling an already enabled root does not emit again.
